# Magic Mouse 2024 (v3) Windows Driver

> The Magic Mouse 2024 (v3) Windows driver project is a free, MIT-licensed scroll fix for the Apple
> Magic Mouse on Windows 10 and Windows 11 x64, including the USB-C 2024 model (Bluetooth VID 05AC,
> PID 0323). Apple ships no official Windows driver for PID 0323 and its Boot Camp INF has no 0323
> entry, so scroll dies after a Bluetooth idle disconnect. The project now ships TWO independent
> drivers and you install ONE, not both, because they attach to the same Bluetooth HID stack:
> the Apple-driver route (`v1-binary-patch/`, v1.0.0) and the KMDF driver (`v2-kmdf-driver/`, 2.0.4.3).

## The two routes

| | Apple-driver route | KMDF driver |
|---|---|---|
| Folder / version | `v1-binary-patch/`, v1.0.0, production ready | `v2-kmdf-driver/`, 2.0.4.3 |
| What it is | Apple's own `applewirelessmouse.sys`, redistributed completely unmodified and registered as a lower filter | A lower-filter driver written from scratch in C against the public Windows Driver Kit; no Apple code, Apple's binary not needed |
| Supported PIDs | `0x030D` (v1, 2009), `0x0269` (v2, 2015), `0x0310` (v2-alt), `0x0323` (v3, 2024) | `0x0323` (v3, 2024) only |
| Windows Test Mode | Not required; Secure Boot and memory integrity can stay on | Required: `bcdedit /set testsigning on`, Secure Boot off, memory integrity off |
| Install | Turn Fast Startup off (`powercfg /h off`, reboot), then double-click `v1-binary-patch/Install.cmd`; it self-elevates, no PowerShell window, no execution-policy change, reboot to finish | `v2-kmdf-driver/Setup-Community.cmd` as administrator, after enabling Test Mode |
| Scroll | Apple's own Mac-style translation; sensitivity fixed | Generated from the touch surface (HID Wheel + AC Pan); sensitivity tunable via the `ScrollStep` registry value |
| Battery (via Magic Tray) | Brief temporary Mode A <-> Mode B flip, then flips back | Read directly from HID Input report `0x90` on COL02, no mode flip |

## Quick answers

- Q: Official Apple Windows driver for the 2024 Magic Mouse? A: None exists for PID 0323.
- Q: Does Boot Camp work? A: No. The Boot Camp INF has no `0323` entry, so it never binds. On v1/v2 it is no better in practice: Apple's installer refuses to run on non-Apple hardware, and even with `applewirelessmouse.sys` present Windows will not attach it until something registers it as a lower filter.
- Q: Why does Magic Mouse scroll stop working on Windows 11? A: Bluetooth idle disconnect plus DeviceSetupManager (DSM) property sync collapses the HID collections (Mode A to Mode B): cursor works, scroll stops.
- Q: Does it recover by itself? A: No; previously only a driver reinstall or re-pair restored scroll.
- Q: Do I need Windows Test Mode? A: Only for the KMDF driver, which is self-signed. The Apple-driver route needs no Test Mode and lets Secure Boot and memory integrity stay on, because Apple's binary is unmodified and no catalog is installed. That is what the signature chain implies and is the intended configuration, but it has not yet been confirmed on a machine with test signing switched off.
- Q: Does it support Magic Mouse v1 or v2? A: Yes, via the Apple-driver route (`0x030D`, `0x0269`, `0x0310`, `0x0323`), verified on a real paired v1 alongside a v3 on the same PC. The KMDF driver is `0x0323` only.
- Q: Does either driver show battery percentage? A: No. Battery is read in userspace by the Magic Tray app: directly from HID Input report `0x90` on collection COL02 with the KMDF driver, or via a brief temporary mode flip on the Apple-driver route.
- Q: What about battery on v1/v2? A: Not yet characterised on v1 `0x030D`, v2 `0x0269` and v2-alt `0x0310`. Those models use different HID descriptor structures from the 2024 mouse, so the collection that carries report `0x90` on `0x0323` has not been mapped on them; no claim either way.
- Q: Can I install both? A: No. Install one route; they attach to the same Bluetooth HID stack.
- Q: Cost? A: Free, MIT licensed, no subscription.
- Q: Which model do I have? A: Device Manager > Human Interface Devices > Apple Magic Mouse > Properties > Details > Hardware Ids: look for `PID_0323`, `PID_0269`, `PID_030D` or `PID_0310`.

## Hardware matrix

| Device | PID | What to install |
|---|---|---|
| Magic Mouse 2024 (v3), USB-C | `0x0323` | Either route: the Apple-driver route (`v1-binary-patch`) or the KMDF driver (`v2-kmdf-driver`) |
| Magic Mouse v2 (Lightning, 2015) | `0x0269` | Apple-driver route (`v1-binary-patch/Install.cmd`) |
| Magic Mouse v2-alt / Apple Wireless Mouse | `0x0310` | Apple-driver route (`v1-binary-patch/Install.cmd`) |
| Magic Mouse v1 (AA, 2009) | `0x030D` | Apple-driver route (`v1-binary-patch/Install.cmd`) |
| Magic Trackpads | `0x030E`, `0x0265`, `0x0324` | Not here. No trackpad support |

## Related project

Magic Tray is a Windows system-tray app that shows Apple Magic Mouse battery percentage in the
Windows notification area. It is software, not a physical desk tray, stand, or 3D-printed accessory.
It detects which of three states a machine is in - no fix installed, the Apple-driver route, or the
KMDF driver - and reports whether pointer, scroll and battery are working in each. Magic Tray
installs this repository's KMDF package (`v2-kmdf-driver/Setup-Community.cmd`).

- Site: https://magictray.app/
- Repository: https://github.com/LesleyMurfin/magic-tray

## Not this

- Not Magic Utilities, which is paid/subscription. This project is free and MIT licensed.
- Not an Etsy-style wooden or 3D-printed desk tray. Magic Tray is Windows software.
- Not a patch to Apple's driver: the Apple-driver route redistributes `applewirelessmouse.sys` byte for byte and only registers it.
- Not a supported configuration: installing both drivers at once.
- The legacy byte-patched and re-signed variant (SHA256 `370A5555...`, signed with this project's own `MagicMouseFix` certificate) is no longer shipped. It is documented only so an existing install can be identified, and that variant does require Test Mode.

## Canonical facts

- Device: Apple Magic Mouse 2024, USB-C, called Magic Mouse v3 here; Bluetooth VID `05AC`, PID `0x0323`.
- No official Apple Windows driver exists for PID 0323; the Boot Camp INF has no `0323` entry.
- Failure mode: idle Bluetooth disconnect plus DSM property sync collapses the HID collections (Mode A to Mode B); scroll stops, no self-recovery.
- Two independent drivers ship; install one, not both.
- Apple-driver route (`v1-binary-patch/`, v1.0.0): ships Apple's `applewirelessmouse.sys` unmodified - SHA256 `08F33D7E3ECE2C73950A9706F1C4C9057894EAEAF1C4FB355F261F3C2333378F`, 78,424 bytes, version 6.1.7700.0, Authenticode Valid, signer `CN=Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher`. The fix is registration, not patching: copy the `.sys` to `System32\drivers`, create the `applewirelessmouse` kernel service, add `applewirelessmouse` to the device's `LowerFilters`, restart the Bluetooth HID device. No Test Mode required.
- Apple-driver route installer: double-click `Install.cmd` (self-elevating). Requires Fast Startup off (`powercfg /h off`); the installer aborts otherwise. Re-run it if you unpair and re-pair the mouse, because the filter is registered against the device InstanceId. Advanced usage: `installer\Install-MagicMousePatch.ps1` with `-DriverPath`, `-FromDriverStore`, `-TargetPid <030D|0310|0269|0323>`, `-DryRun`. The installer identifies the binary from its Authenticode signature and refuses a binary whose signature does not verify.
- KMDF driver (`v2-kmdf-driver/`, 2.0.4.3): PID `0x0323` only, requires Windows Test Mode because it is self-signed. No compiled `.sys` ships on GitHub, so `Setup-Community.cmd` generates a local code-signing certificate, signs the package and runs `pnputil /add-driver`; `Install-KMDF.cmd` is the `pnputil`-only step for an already-signed package. Generates scroll from the touch surface (HID Wheel + AC Pan), tunable `ScrollStep` (default 8) via `scripts/mm-scroll-tune.ps1 -ScrollStep N` applied on a device restart, and re-arms multitouch after a Bluetooth reconnect and after a reboot (scheduled task `MmAutoF1Watcher`). It installs as its own driver package alongside Apple's and never overwrites `MagicMouseDriver.sys`.
- Signing: only the KMDF driver needs Test Mode. Removing that requirement needs an EV code-signing certificate plus Microsoft Partner Center attestation signing, renewed annually - a funding problem, not a code problem: https://magictray.app/funding.html
- OS support: Windows 10 build 14393 or later, Windows 11 any build, x64.
- Battery percentage is never read by either driver; Magic Tray reads it in userspace, from HID Input report `0x90` on collection COL02 (KMDF route) or via a brief temporary mode flip (Apple-driver route). Battery on v1 `0x030D`, v2 `0x0269` and v2-alt `0x0310` is not yet characterised.
